pr_title: [ESQL] Add warnings on STATS alias collisions
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/114970

Added the warnings in the `RemoveStatsOverride` LogicalPlan rule, which is the same one that's removing the duplicates.

Also, fixed the groupings parser, which was assigning, to each stats grouping field, the source of the full "grouping context" instead. Without this fix, the warnings on groupings would, in some cases, say something like `Line 2:10: Field 'x' shadowed by field at line 2:10`.

As there are already tests for these cases, I'm requiring the capability on them, and updating their warnings expectations.

## Notes
I'm treating this as an enhancement instead of a bug. As there's existing logic removing duplicates, I'll guess this was decided at some point (Decision that may apply more or less nowadays).
And still, solving it this way is less dangerous and doesn't break compatibility.

issue_context.title: ES|QL: Alias collisions in STATS
issue_context.body:
```
row x = 1, y = 2 | stats y = max(x) by y
```

In this case, STATS cannot return both the aggregate `y = max(x)` and the grouping `y`, because they have the same alias.

Surprisingly, it returns the grouping:

```
       y       
---------------
2              
```

Not sure if a query like this should be invalid, but if it's valid, the aggregate is probably more relevant.

I'm labeling it as a bug, but I'm not completely sure.
comments:
Same for 

```
row x = 1, `max(x)` = 2 | stats max(x) by `max(x)`
```

```
    max(x)     
---------------
2              
```

Hm, I agree that the behavior can be unexpected, but I don't know if this can be improved. I don't think it's a bug in the implementation.

Currently, we just go left-to-right over all expressions in the `STATS` and duplicate names get shadowed by expressions further to the right.

```
row x = 1, y = 2 | stats y = max(x) by y
```
It's reasonable to assume that this will return 2 columns, and in this case it's not even ambiguous what they should be: `by y` can only refer to the `y` defined in the `row` command.

But we cannot have 2 columns with the same name in the output of the command, so we can return either the `y = max(x)` or the `y` from `by y`.

```
row x = 1, `max(x)` = 2 | stats max(x) by `max(x)`
```
This has the same problem.

Since shadowing doesn't really add value to the `STATS` command, it'd be reasonable to consider such queries simply invalid. But we can't fail them now as this would be breaking bwc.

We can send a warning though as users probably didn't want to write such a query in the first place.

review_comments:
This was originally replacing the "Line 1:X:" text to the new position after the `FROM index` update. I'm modifying it to replace any `1:X`.
The fix currently works, and I can't think of any obvious case where this will fail in the near future, as `X:Y` is a quite specific string
